transcript.text:
I can help with that. 'Not working' usually points to one of three things: no power getting to the machine, the door not being recognised as closed (so it won't start), or an internal fault. First, let's rule out the basics:
1. Check the plug and socket: Is the dryer firmly plugged in? If there is a switch on the plug, is it on? Try plugging another appliance into that socket to see if it works (this suggests if the power is actually reaching the machine).
2. Check the door: Open and shut the door firmly. Does it click or latch properly? Many dryers will not start at all if they think the door is open.
3. Listen/Watch: When you press 'Start', do any lights illuminate on the display, or do you hear a faint hum or relay click? If there is absolutely no sign of life (no lights, no sound), it is probably a power issue (socket, plug, or internal fuse). Please let me know what happens when you try to start it with the door closed.
Plug and socket are fine, the lights come on. But when I press start nothing happens, no sound at all. The door doesn't click shut, it swings back slightly open.

Because the lights come on but nothing happens when you press start—and crucially because the door doesn't latch properly—the machine's safety system thinks the door is open. It will not run if it doesn't detect a closed door. We need to separate whether this is a mechanical issue (the handle or catch is broken so the door physically won't shut) or an electrical one (the switch that detects the door is shut has failed). Please unplug the dryer first. Then:
1. Look at the latch on the door and the slot it goes into. Is the plastic piece broken, cracked, or missing? Is anything stuck in there?
2. Look inside the door frame (where the door meets the cabinet). Do you see a small button or lever that gets pushed in when the door is shut? If the catch is broken, we need to replace the handle/catch assembly. If it looks intact but the machine still won't start even if you hold that internal switch down (carefully), then the switch itself has likely failed.
Yes the plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, found the piece on the floor. If I hold the door firmly shut and press start it runs, but stops when I let go.

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
That suggests it: the plastic tongue (the catch) has snapped off. The door cannot latch properly, so the safety switch never engages and the dryer won't start unless you hold it shut. This is a mechanical fault, not an electrical one. The fix is to replace the door handle/catch assembly. To find the right part for your machine, I need the make and model number. This is usually on a sticker inside the door opening or on the back of the unit. Do you have that to hand?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
Not off the top of my head, it's a Hotpoint. I can read it from the sticker inside the door recess if you need it - is that where it is?

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
Yes, that is exactly where it is. The sticker inside the door opening (or sometimes on the back of the machine) will have the specific model number we need to find the correct replacement part. To confirm what we've found: because the plastic tongue has snapped off, the door cannot latch properly. The fix is to replace the door handle/catch assembly. Once I have the model number, I can tell you exactly which part you need and how to fit it.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok, I'll go and read it off the sticker now. Is it the long code on there, or something else?

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
It’s usually a shorter alphanumeric code, often starting with a letter and numbers (for example, something like 'WML...' or 'TDC...'). The long string is typically the serial number, which isn't needed for finding the part. Just read out the model code exactly as it appears.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok, I'm looking at it now. I'll read out whatever the model code says in a sec. Is there anything else I need to do first?

[Heading: Likely cause: door switch]
No, there is nothing else you need to do right now. Just take your time reading the model code when you are ready. To confirm where we are: because the plastic tongue has snapped off, the door cannot latch properly. The fix is to replace the door handle/catch assembly. Once I have the model number, I can tell you exactly which part you need and how to fit it.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

Door not latched or door switch fault (medium)
plan: The fault they reported is: "not working". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
